Maybe we'll need to tweak the code review incentive. Seems a bit high? 
I think we need to make sure that linguist generated ignored files are NOT included in line count 
gentlementlegen got credit for reviewing 9000 added lines but the net result is there was only 6000 added so something might be wrong there too. Also they only left one review but got credited twice. 
I think when merging you get credited for code review again which might not be correct.
Hey guys @shiv810 @gentlementlegen we don't have any information displayed on this in the scoring summary? That should have been a requirement! How do we know if its even working now?
This should be prioritized

This seems a lot more interesting compared to word count but we should test. 
_Originally posted by @0x4007 in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/97#issuecomment-2363145914_
We can use an npm package to do most of the work, but I think that tweaking the weighting of the output of this module might take time to get right, which is why I made the time 4 hours instead of something like 1 hour. 
As an extension of this, if it is successful, then we can consider removing word counting from the scoring criteria, and instead use the amount of html tags as a proxy for comment length. 
For example, a comment with many list items, images, and links is more likely to be "longer" than a comment without. This may place the emphasis on higher Flesch Reading Ease (more easily understandable) and useful elements (images, links) vs writing verbose comments with low information density etc.
Do you have any QA?
Seems mostly fine. Small tweaks requested but not show stopping

I'm not sure of the best approach for score weighting. But I have a feeling that we will remove word counter and have html tag counting plus this flesch kincaid scoring cover the "quantitative" scoring

@gentlementlegen we will need to run some tests to tweak the following:
1. Remove word counter
2. Remove ^0.85 exponent
3. Increase weight of readability scoring
4. Decrease weight of html formatting scoring 
Hope to run on historical comments and try to get similar results. I wish there was an algorithm we could make to automatically calibrate new changes to be similar to old scoring.
Isn't 60 kind of low? How did you come to this number @shiv810
@shiv810 i agree with `targetReadabilityScore` please fix
"60.0–50.0	10th to 12th grade	Fairly difficult to read." In the context of the other descriptions I think this is the best choice, yes.
If it's not too complicated then yes sounds like a good idea

That's pretty intense
In the future you need to link a pull immediately after starting.

I thought the scoring should be normalized 0-100 
Why not use another implementation from npm packages?

The spec says ease is normalized 0-100. Perhaps the implementation you did is not correct. 
For clarification I got the idea from ChatGPT and never implemented this idea before so I don't know for sure, but I think a hallucination is unlikely.

I just noticed you did normalize the scores sorry for missing that earlier. 
I just hope the implementation is correct. It is unexpected that you did it custom.

Permit html? 
We don't run this on bot comments so it's not applicable.
